Accessibility

Part of the system, not a finishing touch.

How to use the brand accessibly across websites, presentations, reports, PDFs, social graphics and email signatures. The target is WCAG 2.2 AA, with AAA contrast wherever the palette allows it.

Download the guidance (PDF) ↓

Guiding principle

In short

Accessibility is part of the design system, not a finishing touch. Brand colours and visual treatments should never make information harder to read, understand or use.

1. Contrast-safe colour combinations

WCAG 2.2 AA is the baseline.

  • Normal text: a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.
  • Large text: at least 3:1 (about 24 CSS px regular, or 18.7 CSS px bold).
  • Meaningful graphics and UI components: at least 3:1 against adjacent colours.
  • Non-colour cues: colour must never be the only way information, status or meaning is communicated.

  • Aa

    Ink on Warm White

    Recommended default for light layouts.

    ✓ Pass · 15.92:1

  • Aa

    Ink on Teal

    Recommended for teal highlights and buttons with dark text.

    ✓ Pass · 8.45:1

  • Aa

    Teal on Warm White

    Do not use teal for text on Warm White.

    ✕ Fail · 1.88:1

  • Aa

    Ink on White

    Suitable for clean, high-contrast documents.

    ✓ Pass · 19.13:1

Ratios are calculated with the WCAG relative-luminance method when the site is built. Treat accent pairings as starting points and test every real use. See the full matrix.

Recommended colour rules

Which colour, where.

Context and recommended treatment
Context / useRecommended treatment
Main body textInk (#0B0F1A) on Warm White (#EDEAE3) or white (#FFFFFF)
Dark-mode body textWarm White (#EDEAE3) on Ink (#0B0F1A)
Secondary text on darkMist (#9AA4B8) on Ink, Card or Lift; Haze (#8A98B2) on Ink or Card
Links and accents on darkTeal (#00C2A8) on Ink or Card, with an underline on links in running text
Buttons and filled highlightsInk text on a Teal, Amber or other accent fill
Anything on lightInk text only. Accents appear as fills with Ink text, never as text, lines or icons
Status and categoryColour plus a written label. Never colour alone

2. Typography and layout

Text that survives stress.

  • Size and weight

    Body text is 16px (1rem) or larger, in rem so it scales. Below 24px use weight 400 or heavier.

  • Line length and spacing

    Columns of 60–72 characters, line height of 1.6 or more, and space between paragraphs. Content must survive WCAG text-spacing overrides.

  • Structure

    One h1, headings in order, lists as lists, tables with captions and header cells. Don’t use headings for size.

  • Reflow and zoom

    No horizontal scrolling at 320px wide or 400% zoom, except for data tables and code in their own scroll region.

  • Capitals

    Short uppercase labels are fine with wide tracking. Never set sentences or long headings in all caps.

  • Language

    Plain language, short sentences, descriptive link text. Spell out acronyms on first use. Set the page language.

3. Interaction

Easy to reach, easy to see.

  • Focus: a 3px ring in #7FE6D4 with a 4px offset on every interactive element (12.9:1 on Ink). Never remove outlines without a replacement.
  • Targets: 44 × 44 px minimum, and never below the 24 × 24 px WCAG 2.2 floor.
  • Skip link as the first focusable element; keyboard order matches reading order.
  • No hover-only content. Anything revealed on hover must also appear on focus and tap.
  • Forced colours: keep a visible border on buttons so they survive Windows High Contrast.

4. Motion and media

Calm by default, controllable always.

  • Honour prefers-reduced-motion: stop animation and smooth scrolling.
  • Nothing flashes more than three times a second. Nothing autoplays with sound.
  • Decorative motion over five seconds gets a pause control, or is removed.
  • Video: captions, a transcript, and no information carried by sound alone.

5. Documents, slides, social and email

Same rules, every format.

  • PDFs and reports

    Tagged PDF, document title and language, real headings, reading order, alt text. Ink on Warm White.

  • Presentations

    24 pt body minimum, one idea per slide, unique slide titles, alt text, and no meaning carried by colour alone.

  • Social graphics

    Short headline in the image, full message in the post text, alt text on every image, captions on video.

  • Email and signatures

    Live text for names and links, Ink logo with alt text, no contact details inside images, links that name their destination.

Checklist

Before you publish.

  • ☐Normal text is at least 4.5:1; large text and graphics at least 3:1, measured on the real background.
  • ☐Hover, focus, disabled states and text over images or tints have been checked too.
  • ☐Nothing relies on colour alone: status, links, charts and errors also use text, shape or an icon.
  • ☐Headings are real headings, in order, and each page has one h1.
  • ☐Links say where they go. No “click here”; external and download links are flagged.
  • ☐Everything works by keyboard, with a visible 3px focus ring and a skip link on pages with navigation.
  • ☐Touch targets are at least 44 × 44 px (never below 24 × 24).
  • ☐Images have alt text that says what they show; decorative images have an empty alt.
  • ☐Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion, and anything moving for over five seconds can be paused.
  • ☐Video has captions and a transcript; audio has a transcript.
  • ☐The page reflows at 320px wide and at 400% zoom with no sideways scroll; text size is in rem.
  • ☐PDFs are tagged, with a title, language and reading order. Slides use real titles and alt text.
